newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares close up on speculation, Sampoerna.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares close up on speculation, Sampoerna.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended up on Thursday on speculative buying of some secondliners coupled with bargain-hunting on cigarette maker Sampoerna, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 1.61 points, or 0.28 percent, to close at 567.93 points after hitting a high of 569.06 points. Gainers led losers by 57 to 48, with 58 counters unchanged.
"I don't expect any big surprise which could lead to fresh buying on Friday. The market is likely to be stagnant as overall sentiment remains weak," said one foreign broker.
Sampoerna, which had fallen steeply earlier in the week, is likely to continue in focus after its rebound, brokers said.
They said the rebound was the main reason for the day's overall index rise, but market sentiment was poor because support from regional markets was limited.
Sampoerna rose 5.87 percent to 19,375 rupiah, with about 1.4 million shares changing hands, after hitting an intra-day high of 19,800 rupiah.

Brokers said the the upside of Sampoerna was limited as investors remain cautious about its purchase of a stake in automobile manufacturer Astra International and the reason for a new $400 million loan which the company announced on Saturday.
They also said the rise was largely supported by local buyers and some foreigners on the perception that the share was oversold.
Brokers said some local players were also buying speculatively on certain small-capitalised stocks mostly for short-term gains.
Property firm Surya Dutamakmur topped the active list with 6.5 million shares traded, rising 50 rupiah to 650 rupiah. Brokers ascribed the rise to prevailing cheap prices.
Hotel Sahid Jaya was also actively traded on a turnover of 5.9 million shares, falling 50 rupiah to 1,100 on local-led profit taking after earlier gains.
It rose to 1,250 rupiah earlier on market talk of a possible takeover and a rights issue.
A company official denied the firm could be target of a takeover but said it was considering a rights issue to finance an expansion plan.
